story.title: DoorDash is acquiring Instacart for $17 billion
story.summary: DoorDash has announced plans to acquire Instacart in a deal valued at approximately $17 billion. This acquisition aims to combine DoorDash's strength in restaurant delivery with Instacart's grocery delivery services, potentially enhancing customer options for food delivery. The deal is expected to close in late 2027 or early 2028.

explore_lenses.label: Why does the combination matter for shoppers?
explore_lenses.title: A larger delivery and retail platform
explore_lenses.summary: The companies say the deal would combine DoorDash's logistics network with Instacart's grocery technology and retailer relationships. The potential consumer benefits are company projections, while the combination would also concentrate shopping and delivery data.

claims.text: DoorDash says Instacart customers could gain access to more than 50,000 additional stores beyond the nearly 100,000 stores already on Instacart's platform.
DoorDash projects that combining DashPass and Instacart+ could save members an estimated $100 million a year in membership fees; this is a company forecast, not a guaranteed consumer outcome.
Groundwork Collaborative President Lindsay Owens argues that the transaction would consolidate extensive consumer-shopping data and pricing technology in one company.

explore_lenses.label: How did the companies reach this deal?
explore_lenses.title: Grocery capability meets delivery scale
explore_lenses.summary: Instacart brings a large grocery-retail technology network, while DoorDash has been expanding beyond restaurant delivery. The $65-per-share offer is structured as mostly cash with an optional stock component for Instacart shareholders.

claims.text: Instacart says it partners with more than 2,200 retail banners representing nearly 100,000 stores, across its marketplace, enterprise technology and advertising businesses.
DoorDash offered $65 per Instacart share, which it says was a 26% premium to Instacart's October 22, 2026 closing price, before media reports of a possible transaction.
Tony Xu, DoorDash's CEO, says the strategic rationale is to pair Instacart's grocery expertise with DoorDash's delivery network and local-store technology.
Reuters reports that eMarketer analyst Zak Stambor views the acquisition as a shortcut for DoorDash into grocery, where it has long sought to grow.

explore_lenses.label: What must happen before it can close?
explore_lenses.title: Shareholder and regulatory review remain
explore_lenses.summary: The agreement is signed but not completed. It requires an Instacart shareholder vote and antitrust-related and other regulatory clearances, while both firms are also subjects of a separate FTC information-gathering inquiry on personalized pricing and worker compensation.

claims.text: DoorDash expects the transaction to close at the end of 2027 or in the first half of 2028, subject to Instacart shareholder approval, the Hart-Scott-Rodino waiting period, regulatory approvals including in Canada and Israel, and customary closing conditions.
Holders of about 19% of Instacart's outstanding shares have agreed to vote for the deal, but that does not itself complete the required shareholder approval.

The FTC has ordered DoorDash and Instacart, among other companies, to provide information for a study of whether personal data affects individualized prices for consumers or compensation for gig workers.
eMarketer analyst Zak Stambor forecasts that the overlap in grocery delivery makes antitrust scrutiny highly likely; that is an analyst assessment rather than an announced enforcement action.

story_report.summary: DoorDash plans to acquire Instacart in a transaction valued at about $17 billion, bringing together two major delivery companies. The proposed deal would expand DoorDash’s position in grocery delivery while pairing it with Instacart’s retail marketplace, technology and advertising operations. The companies expect the transaction to close at the end of 2027 or during the first half of 2028, but it remains subject to shareholder approval, regulatory reviews and other closing conditions.

sections.heading: Customer Choices and Membership Plans
sections.body: DoorDash says Instacart customers could gain access to more than 50,000 additional stores beyond the nearly 100,000 stores already on Instacart’s platform. It also projects that combining DashPass and Instacart+ could save members an estimated $100 million annually in membership fees. Those are company projections, however, and broader store access or unified memberships do not necessarily mean lower total checkout costs.

sections.heading: Instacart’s Retail Network and Offer
sections.body: Instacart says it works with more than 2,200 retail banners representing nearly 100,000 stores across its marketplace, enterprise technology and advertising businesses. DoorDash offered $65 per Instacart share, which it says represented a 26% premium to Instacart’s Oct. 22, 2026 closing price before media reports of a possible deal. DoorDash Chief Executive Tony Xu said the combination would pair Instacart’s grocery expertise with DoorDash’s delivery network and local-store technology.

sections.heading: Approvals and Regulatory Review
sections.body: The acquisition requires Instacart shareholder approval, the expiration of the Hart-Scott-Rodino waiting period, regulatory approvals including in Canada and Israel, and customary closing conditions. Holders of about 19% of Instacart’s outstanding shares have agreed to support the deal, though that alone does not satisfy the shareholder vote requirement. Separately, the Federal Trade Commission has required DoorDash and Instacart, among other companies, to provide information for an inquiry into whether personal data affects individualized consumer prices or gig-worker compensation.

unresolved.text: Whether the combined company’s store selection and membership plans result in lower overall costs for consumers will depend on post-close pricing, fees and retailer participation.
No regulator had publicly announced a merger challenge or remedy as of Oct. 29, 2026; the duration and outcome of regulatory review remain unresolved.

related_stories.title: Milwaukee Brewers Capture First World Series Title by Defeating Rays 4-1
related_stories.summary: The Milwaukee Brewers have won their first World Series title in franchise history, defeating the Tampa Bay Rays 4-1 in Game 5. This victory marks the culmination of nearly six decades of aspirations for the team, which was founded as an expansion franchise 57 years ago. The decisive game took place at Tropicana Field in Tampa, celebrating a significant achievement for the Brewers and their fans.

related_stories.title: King Charles III Dances with Locals During Bahamas Visit
related_stories.summary: King Charles III participated in a vibrant Junkanoo street parade in Nassau, Bahamas, on October 28, showcasing his dance skills. This event marks his first Caribbean tour since ascending to the throne, during which he acknowledged the historical suffering of the region.

related_stories.title: Dolores Huerta, Pioneering Labor Leader and Civil Rights Icon, Dies at 96
related_stories.summary: Dolores Huerta, a prominent labor leader and civil rights activist, passed away at the age of 96 from cancer at her home in Bakersfield, California. She was known for co-founding the United Farm Workers alongside Cesar Chavez and for her significant contributions to labor rights and feminist movements. Huerta died surrounded by her close family.

related_stories.summary: As early voting progresses in South Carolina, over 671,000 residents have cast their ballots, though current totals do not indicate a clear leader in the Senate race. The early voting data reflects a broader trend, with more than 42 million Americans participating in early voting nationwide, suggesting heightened enthusiasm ahead of the midterm elections.
